key_insight: A Policy Compiler (PCAS) deterministically enforces complex authorization policies for LLM-based agents by compiling high-level rules into runtime-enforceable primitives and tracking information flow beyond linear message histories.
problem_solved: LLM agents often operate under complex authorization and compliance constraints, but embedding policies in prompts gives no enforcement guarantees and linear conversation histories fail to capture cross-agent information flow and provenance needed for correct enforcement.
method: Specify high-level authorization and compliance policies and compile them into concrete, monitorable enforcement primitives (runtime checks, guards, and constrained actions).
Model and track information flow across agents as a provenance/graph structure (not just a linear message log) to capture branching, merges, and cross-agent dependencies.
Enforce policies deterministically at runtime via compiled monitors and constrained execution, enabling provable guarantees about allowed actions and data disclosures.
impact: PCAS lets practitioners deploy agentic systems with stronger, deterministic guarantees for authorization, data-exposure prevention, and regulatory compliance—reducing risk from latent prompt-based policies and subtle multi-agent flows.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: Policy authoring → Policy compiler → Runtime monitors → Agent ecosystem (showing enforcement points).
Information-flow graph vs. linear history: side-by-side illustration showing how graph provenance captures branching and merges across agents.
Compilation pipeline flowchart: high-level policy → intermediate representation → enforcement primitives/monitors → runtime enforcement example.
Iconography: shield/padlock for security, graph nodes for provenance, gavel/document for compliance.
paper_title: Policy Compiler for Secure Agentic Systems
paper_authors: Nils Palumbo, Sarthak Choudhary, Jihye Choi, Prasad Chalasani, Mihai Christodorescu
